**Summary**

I researched Apple's most recent results and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit price of $222.70 (filled at $222.70, total ≈ $9,798.80), which is inside my mandate: AAPL is an eligible name, it's a buy, it's under the $10,000 per-order cap, today's total of $9,798.80 is well under the $20,000 daily cap, the limit was set at the current market price ($222.70 last, with a $222.68/$222.72 bid-ask at 15:05 UTC on 2024-11-06), and no money left the account (funded from $50,000 cash, leaving the 100 MSFT shares untouched). The case for buying rests on Apple's fiscal 2024 fourth-quarter release (quarter ended September 28, 2024), which reported quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, and — the figure named in the task — **total net sales for fiscal 2024 of $391.0 billion**, with net income of $93.7 billion, or $6.08 per diluted share, despite a one-time $10.2 billion income tax charge. I verified that $391.0 billion against Apple's fiscal 2024 Form 10-K filed 2024-11-01, which shows total net sales of $391,035 million (the figure I cited in key_figures on the order), along with net income of $93,736 million and diluted EPS of $6.08. The combination of returning revenue growth, a full-year record top line near $391 billion, and continued earnings power supports a modest starter position, so I limited the purchase to one small order rather than committing the full daily allowance.
